name: overhead-from-the-top
prompt: Vertical 9:16 night photograph shot from the summit of a giant column of piled office paper, the lens pointing ninety degrees straight down its side. In the bottom-near foreground the top page lies flat under the camera, perfectly sharp, printed with THE RULES in heavy black block capitals. Beyond its edge the stack falls away as a sheer pale wall of compressed page edges, converging steeply in an ultra-wide 16mm perspective to a puddled concrete warehouse floor far below. Down there five small figures, a little soft, stand close together with their heads thrown back so their faces point up at us. They wear ordinary clothes from a British high street this year: a hoodie under a puffer jacket, a hi-vis work vest, a black rain shell, joggers, trainers and boots, thick gloves on both hands with sleeves pulled over the wrists, collars zipped up to the jaw. Over every head is a close wool hood, blank where a face should be, and every hood is its own deep shade: navy, bottle green, charcoal, oxblood, black. Sewn onto each hood is a broad white hoop that encircles the face, and within that hoop one red triangle is placed up near the top of the hoop on the side of the wearer's left eye socket, so to us it shows on the right-hand side of the mask, never in the middle. Only wool and stitching, nothing hard or glowing. The figures hold small torches aimed up the paper cliff, and nothing else in the room is bright: the beams cut pale shafts through floating dust, throwing white blooms onto the page edges and making the white rings and red triangles flash. A weak orange sodium haze leaks in from a tiny window high on the far wall and touches one flank of the stack. Beyond those beams the warehouse drowns in black, with wet glints on the floor. Night, high contrast, visible film grain, a dizzying drop seen from the top.
